question: Bushu, Yemshe and Tokhu Emong are some of the cultural festivals celebrated by the tribal people of which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagaland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bushu, Yemshe, and Tokhu Emong** are major cultural festivals celebrated by the tribal communities of Nagaland.
 
• **Tokhu Emong** is celebrated by the Lotha Naga tribe as a post-harvest festival to mark the end of the agricultural season.
 
• **Bushu** is a festival of the Kachari tribe, celebrated to mark the end of the paddy cultivation cycle.
 
• **Yemshe** is observed by the Pochury tribe as a harvest festival, signifying a time of joy and thanksgiving.
 
• Nagaland is known as the **‘Land of Festivals’** due to its diverse tribal communities, each having unique cultural practices and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagaland's Tribal Diversity**

 
 
• Nagaland is home to 16 major tribes, including Ao, Angami, Sumi, Lotha, Chakhesang, and Konyak tribes, among others.
 
• Each tribe has its unique dialect, attire, customs, and festivals, contributing to the state's rich cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Hornbill Festival**
 
 
• This is the most famous cultural festival of Nagaland, celebrated annually in December.
 
• It showcases the cultural vibrancy of all tribes and is often referred to as the **‘Festival of Festivals’**.
 
• The festival includes traditional dance, music, handicrafts, and cuisine, attracting tourists from around the world.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Nagaland**
 
 
• Nagaland is located in Northeast India and shares its borders with Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, and Myanmar.
 
• Kohima is the state capital, while Dimapur is the largest city and a major commercial hub.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Practices**
 
 
• Many festivals in Nagaland are closely linked to agricultural cycles, emphasizing the importance of farming in their livelihood.
 
• Traditional attire, dances, and songs during festivals reflect the deep-rooted cultural identity of the tribes.
